provider.query_method: pg_index + pg_get_indexdef + independent row-number/OID and constraint, class, method, stats metadata; read only
provider.privacy: no auth identities, member rows, tokens, shots, notes or private logs read

coverage.next_cursor: pg_catalog.pg_index: remaining outside private/public/auth schemas, next schema alphabetically; obtain fresh counts/previous receipts first

methods: Independently read each full provider reconstructed CREATE INDEX declaration and examined column/expression, uniqueness, access method, predicate and order, type and caller class
Cross-checked exact internal index key, operator class, collation, option, predicate and distinct OIDs for candidate overlapping indexes
Used read-only FK/constraint dependencies, scan and index-byte metadata as supporting evidence, not as evidence of disuse
Auth schema is Supabase platform-managed and owned by #96; no live index/DDL changes, no user records or credentials inspected

findings.mechanism: Both B-tree on precisely identifier, same indkey/opclass/collation/option, no predicate; UNIQUE variant can support same lookup plus enforces uniqueness. Nonunique copy is not constraint-backed.
findings.reason: Platform-managed Auth schema and unknown upstream migration/upgrade owner; source/deployment lifecycle and dynamic provider use not proven. Do not modify Auth DDL or create a DIC migration.
SSO predicate changes uniqueness coverage; full email lookup and partial non-SSO uniqueness not byte-identical.
Unconditional unique identity constraint and revoked_at IS NULL partial access path differ.

findings.details: Original platform migrations, full hosted Auth runtime callers, per-query performance traces and upstream ownership. Scan counts of zero are not proof of dead use.

checks.cross_issue: #96 Auth owns functional/authentication acceptance; #267 alone owns GitHub source line review
